airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway by being a discrete aircraft object rather than a long paved strip, from airport by lacking broad terminal-scale aviation surroundings, and from parking_lot by lacking organized vehicle-row layout.
airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways and airport-related infrastructure, distinguishing airport from runway by broader aviation context, from airplane by lacking a single compact fuselage object, and from industrial_area by emphasizing aviation pavement rather than factory compounds.
baseball_diamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield and surrounding outfield, distinguishing baseball_diamond from golf_course by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated trailer-like housing rows, and from ground_track_field by lacking an oval running-track pattern.
basketball_court: small rectangular hard-court surface with clear sports markings, distinguishing basketball_court from tennis_court by court layout and line pattern, from parking_lot by lacking vehicle-row organization, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated roof-and-street neighborhood structure.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from island by lacking a fully isolated landmass, from desert by direct water contact, and from lake by coastal shoreline appearance rather than enclosed inland water.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from overpass by weaker elevated road-over-road junction pattern, from freeway by lacking a long continuous multi-lane corridor, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip context.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from desert by slightly richer vegetation texture, from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, and from mountain by weaker terrain relief and shadow structure.
church: prominent religious building or complex with distinctive landmark-like architecture, distinguishing church from palace by less expansive ceremonial layout, from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns, and from basketball_court by lacking small court geometry and line markings.
circular_farmland: cultivated land with large regular circular irrigation patterns, distinguishing circular_farmland from rectangular_farmland by round parcel geometry, from storage_tank by broader agricultural texture around circles, and from wetland by lacking mixed water-vegetation fragmentation.
cloud: bright amorphous atmospheric mass with soft edges and no stable ground texture, distinguishing cloud from lake by lacking a stable enclosed water boundary, from snowberg by softer irregular boundaries and less landform relief, and from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular parcel structure.
commercial_area: dense urban business district with organized building blocks, roads, and large man-made structures, distinguishing commercial_area from industrial_area by lacking heavy factory compounds, from palace by weaker landmark-like symmetry, and from intersection by broader urban building context rather than a compact road node.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense_residential from medium_residential by much closer building intervals, from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row organization, and from commercial_area by smaller repeated residential roofs rather than larger business blocks.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from chaparral by weaker shrub texture, from mountain by less terrain relief, and from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular parcel boundaries, from chaparral by stronger canopy continuity, and from wetland by weaker visible water fragmentation.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous linear flow and road-network structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended roadway rather than a local elevated crossing, from intersection by lacking a compact junction node, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip markings and airport context.
golf_course: large landscaped green field with fairways, lawns, and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golf_course from baseball_diamond by lacking a compact diamond infield, from meadow by stronger man-made landscaping, and from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy.
ground_track_field: sports venue with an oval running track and central field, distinguishing ground_track_field from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated housing rows, from stadium by weaker enclosure and spectator structure, and from baseball_diamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from ship by broader dock-and-shore context, from parking_lot by clear water-adjacent harbor organization, and from mobile_home_park by lacking repetitive residential rows.
industrial_area: large factory-like compounds with heavy infrastructure, storage yards, and production-oriented layouts, distinguishing industrial_area from parking_lot by stronger factory-compound structure, from storage_tank by not being dominated only by circular tanks, and from thermal_power_station by weaker power-plant-specific structure.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from roundabout by lacking a central circular traffic island, from freeway by being a compact crossing node, and from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated housing units.
island: landmass completely surrounded by water with clear shoreline boundary, distinguishing island from lake by stronger land-water separation, from beach by being an enclosed landform rather than a shoreline strip, and from wetland by clearer solid landmass structure.
lake: large enclosed inland water body with smooth water surface and clear boundary, distinguishing lake from wetland by more uniform open water, from island by water-dominant appearance rather than land enclosed by water, and from cloud by stable ground-level water boundary rather than soft atmospheric texture.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries, from golf_course by weaker designed landscaping, and from ground_track_field by lacking formal sports-field geometry.
medium_residential: moderately spaced residential houses with visible yards and neighborhood streets, distinguishing medium_residential from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row structure, from dense_residential by larger spacing, and from sparse_residential by denser neighborhood grouping.
mobile_home_park: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobile_home_park from medium_residential by stronger trailer-like regularity, from dense_residential by more uniform layout, and from sparse_residential by denser and more systematic placement.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with strong relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from snowberg by less snow-dominant brightness, from desert by stronger terrain relief, and from chaparral by much larger elevation structure.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from bridge by emphasizing road-over-road transport structure.
palace: large landmark complex with symmetrical layout, open courtyards, and prominent architecture, distinguishing palace from church by more expansive ceremonial organization, from commercial_area by weaker dense urban block texture, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns.
parking_lot: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking_lot from industrial_area by lacking dense factory compounds, from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context, and from runway by lacking a long straight aviation strip.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from railway_station by lacking a concentrated station hub, from freeway by rail-line texture rather than paved multi-lane roadway, and from industrial_area by stronger track-line dominance.
railway_station: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railway_station from railway by stronger station-node organization, from industrial_area by clearer rail concentration, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip geometry and airport context.
rectangular_farmland: cultivated land divided into regular rectangular parcels, distinguishing rectangular_farmland from circular_farmland by angular field boundaries, from terrace by lacking stepped contour bands, and from meadow by stronger man-made agricultural organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from industrial_area by natural water geometry rather than factory compounds, from lake by a more linear channel shape, and from island by lacking a fully enclosed landmass.
roundabout: circular traffic junction with a central island and radiating roads, distinguishing roundabout from intersection by the visible circular center, from medium_residential by road-dominant junction geometry, and from tennis_court by lacking sports-court markings.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open airport-like surroundings, distinguishing runway from airport by weaker terminal-scale context, from parking_lot by lacking dense parked-vehicle rows, and from freeway by lacking complex road branching.
sea_ice: bright frozen surface with irregular cracked or slab-like texture over water, distinguishing sea_ice from snowberg by flatter ice-field appearance, from island by lacking stable land texture, and from ship by lacking a discrete vessel shape.
ship: discrete vessel object on water with elongated hull-like structure, distinguishing ship from harbor by lacking broad dock-side context, from island by clear object boundaries and non-land texture, and from industrial_area by being a floating object rather than a land-based factory compound.
snowberg: bright snow- or ice-covered elevated landform with strong cold-tone texture, distinguishing snowberg from sea_ice by stronger landform-like relief, from mountain by stronger snow coverage, and from lake by lacking smooth open-water texture.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse_residential from medium_residential by much larger spacing, from mobile_home_park by lacking uniform trailer-row organization, and from rectangular_farmland by repeated roof structures rather than crop parcels.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from ground_track_field by stronger venue framing, from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated residential rows, and from baseball_diamond by larger scale and more complex sports-facility structure.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage_tank from industrial_area by stronger circular-container dominance, from thermal_power_station by emphasizing tank clusters, and from circular_farmland by compact industrial circles without surrounding crop texture.
tennis_court: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated court geometry, distinguishing tennis_court from medium_residential by lacking roof clusters, from basketball_court by different court layout and line pattern, and from mobile_home_park by lacking trailer-like housing rows.
terrace: stepped agricultural or hillside bands following slope contours, distinguishing terrace from rectangular_farmland by contour-aligned layered structure, from palace by lacking landmark-building symmetry, and from mountain by showing repeated stepped bands rather than broad natural rugged relief.
thermal_power_station: large power-generation complex with heavy industrial structures, chimneys, or cooling-related facilities, distinguishing thermal_power_station from storage_tank by broader power-plant infrastructure, from industrial_area by more plant-specific heavy layout, and from commercial_area by lacking urban business-block organization.
wetland: water-rich natural area with mixed shallow water and vegetation patches, distinguishing wetland from lake by more fragmented water-vegetation texture, from island by lacking a solid enclosed landmass, and from chaparral by stronger visible water presence.
